title: ARIA Attribute Variants
subtopics: Aligning visual state with actual component state
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of aria attribute variants.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on aria attribute variants and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: ARIA Attribute Variants matters because interface appearance should reflect actual state while remaining understandable to keyboard, touch and assistive-technology users.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Styling ARIA states; Expanded and collapsed states; Selected and pressed states; Accessible component styling; Aligning visual state with actual component state. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Complete the linked practical exercise “Interactive FAQ”. Create a minimal example demonstrating aria attribute variants. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to aria attribute variants.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to aria attribute variants.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A centered content section with a prominent heading and readable paragraph; rendering requires the configured Tailwind build.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying aria attribute variants without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: ARIA Attribute Variants is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
